title: PWA enhancements: offline mode, caching, iOS splash, install UX, and standalone layout polish

requirements.summary: Add offline support via a service worker that precaches the app shell and provides a clear offline fallback UI when the network is unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: A service worker is registered by the app and becomes active after first load (with standard update/refresh behavior).
Key static assets required to render the UI shell are precached so that reopening the installed app without network still loads the shell.
When the user is offline, the app shows a clear offline state (e.g., dedicated offline screen or persistent banner) rather than failing silently.
Offline behavior does not require backend changes and does not break authenticated flows when online.

file_operations.description: Implement a service worker that precaches core app-shell assets and provides an offline fallback for navigations when the network is unavailable; include a safe update flow (e.g., activate/claim + cache versioning) so new deployments replace old caches.
Add a simple offline fallback page that clearly explains the app is offline (English text) and that some features require connectivity.
Register the service worker on app startup in production and set up standard update behavior (e.g., detect updated worker and prompt user to refresh or auto-reload safely).
Create a persistent offline/online status banner component that listens to browser connectivity changes and displays a clear offline state without blocking the UI.
Wire OfflineBanner into the main layout so offline state is visible across all routes when the user loses connectivity.

requirements.summary: Improve caching/performance with a smarter service-worker strategy: precache core assets, add runtime caching where safe, and ensure HTML updates are not stuck on stale deployments.
acceptanceCriteria: Core UI assets (HTML/app bundle/CSS and other stable assets) are served quickly on repeat visits via cache.
Runtime caching rules avoid serving stale HTML indefinitely (ensure users still receive new deployments).
Caching strategy does not interfere with Internet Identity authentication flow or canister calls (no caching of authenticated API responses unless explicitly safe).

file_operations.description: Enhance caching rules: use precache for stable assets; use an update-safe navigation strategy (e.g., network-first for navigations with offline fallback) to avoid stale HTML; add runtime caching for static assets (images/fonts) while explicitly bypassing caching for Internet Identity/auth-related requests and canister-call network traffic.

Adjust service worker registration/update handling to ensure new deployments can take effect promptly (e.g., listen for controller changes/updated worker and refresh with clear user control as needed).

requirements.summary: Integrate a custom iOS splash screen with required apple startup image link tags referencing generated static assets.
acceptanceCriteria: `frontend/index.html` includes the appropriate iOS splash/startup image `<link rel="apple-touch-startup-image" ...>` entries referencing generated static assets.
Splash screen assets are stored in `frontend/public/assets/generated` and referenced directly from the frontend (not served through the backend).
When launched from the home screen on iOS, the splash screen displays instead of a blank white/black screen (device support limited to the included sizes).

Add the generated iOS splash screen asset to the public generated assets folder: frontend/public/assets/generated/pwa-splash-ipad-2048x2732.dim_2048x2732.png.

requirements.summary: Implement a better install prompt UX with a visible CTA and iOS guidance when the native install prompt is unavailable, hiding the UX in standalone mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Users who are not installed can discover an install call-to-action without needing to find it incidentally.
When `beforeinstallprompt` is available, the UX triggers the native prompt via the existing hook behavior.
When `beforeinstallprompt` is not available (common on iOS), the UX shows clear English instructions for installing via the browser share/menu flow.
The install UX does not appear when the app is already running in standalone mode.

file_operations.description: Extend the install prompt hook to expose (a) whether the app is running in standalone mode, and (b) platform capability signals (e.g., iOS-like environments without beforeinstallprompt) to drive a unified install CTA that either triggers the native prompt or shows guidance.
Create an install instructions UI (English text) that explains how to install on platforms without a native prompt (e.g., iOS Safari: Share button → Add to Home Screen).

Replace the current install button behavior with a more discoverable install CTA shown whenever the app is not in standalone mode: trigger the native prompt when available, otherwise open the InstallInstructionsDialog; ensure the CTA is not shown in standalone mode.

requirements.summary: Polish standalone layout for native feel by respecting safe-area insets and ensuring stable full-height layout without awkward scrolling/overflow on mobile.
acceptanceCriteria: In standalone mode on mobile, key layout regions (TopBar/Navigation/Main) respect safe-area insets and do not overlap notches/home indicators.
The app avoids unintended double scrollbars and preserves expected full-height layout behavior.
Changes do not require editing files listed as immutable in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.

file_operations.description: Add global safe-area and viewport height handling (e.g., env(safe-area-inset-*) padding helpers, stable 100dvh layout, prevent unintended overflow) to improve standalone behavior on mobile without touching any immutable paths.
Adjust header spacing to respect safe-area inset top in standalone mode (via CSS classes/variables) so the TopBar does not collide with notches/status areas.
Adjust navigation spacing to align with the polished standalone layout and avoid overflow/double scroll scenarios on small mobile screens.

Refine the overall layout structure (min-height/full-height and overflow behavior) so the app maintains a single expected scroll container and respects safe-area insets around main content in standalone mode.
